newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Profit-taking sees Zimbabwe industrials end weak.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking sees Zimbabwe industrials end weak.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares traded mostly softer on Friday, and some analysts predicted the market would continue weaker next week amid profit-taking pressure.

"There are a combination of factors -- some investors are taking a breather to watch the economy and study particular stocks. On the other hand, there are quite a big number of profit-takers in the market," one dealer said in response to a 45.23 points fall in the main industrial index which ended at 6,786.01.
The index closed 204.31 points down on the week.
"The profit-takers in particular are driving some shares down and I think we are going to see this again next week," he added.
Sugar producer Hippo Valley, clothing retailer Truworths and financial group Finhold traded 50 cents down to 750, 100 cents down to 650 and 60 cents down to 940 respectively.
In minings, coal producer Wankie lost 10 cents to 340 and gold miners Falcon plunged 300 cents to 1,500. The secondary seven-share mining index ended 1.40 points down at 1,368.98.
But the mining index was 5.91 points higher on the week.
